features.description: fake_game.py emits HARNESS_LLM/HARNESS_TOOL/RESULT lines from env vars, and run_one.py's pure parsing turns a log into the metrics fields (LLM calls, token sums, median ms, tool calls, repeated tool calls) with tests first.
steps: `public/b/mh_harness/fake_game.py` (stdlib, 3.8-safe) reads FAKE_SLEEP_S (float, default 0), FAKE_WORDS (int, default 2), FAKE_LLM_CALLS (int, default 3), FAKE_EXIT (int, default 0), FAKE_ALARM (string, default empty); for each LLM call i it sleeps FAKE_SLEEP_S/FAKE_LLM_CALLS then prints `HARNESS_LLM {"in": …, "out": …, "ms": …}` and `HARNESS_TOOL {"name": "visit_city", "args": {"city": "city-<i>"}}` (flush=True); when FAKE_ALARM is set it prints one line containing that text after the first call; it ends with `RESULT {"words_found": <FAKE_WORDS>, "score": <int>}` and exits FAKE_EXIT; `FAKE_LLM_CALLS=2 python3 public/b/mh_harness/fake_game.py | grep -c HARNESS_TOOL` prints 2 and `FAKE_EXIT=3 python3 public/b/mh_harness/fake_game.py; echo $?` ends in 3

`public/b/mh_harness/run_one.py` exports `parse_telemetry(log_text)` returning `llm_calls`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `llm_ms_median` (None without calls), `tool_calls`, `repeated_tool_calls` (a call whose name and args JSON-equal an earlier call in the same text); the marker may be anywhere on the line (a timestamp prefix is fine), malformed JSON after a marker is skipped, and `exit_reason(returncode, timed_out, words_found, expected_words)` returns solved / incomplete / timeout / error per spec §3; the module runs nothing on import (`python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "public/b/mh_harness"); import run_one'` prints nothing)

`public/b/mh_harness/tests/test_telemetry.py` has cases: a 3-call log gives llm_calls 3, input_tokens and output_tokens as the sums, llm_ms_median the middle value; 4 tool lines with two identical name+args give tool_calls 4 and repeated_tool_calls 1 (same name, different args is not a repeat); a prefixed line and a malformed JSON line; exit_reason for the four cases (returncode 0 and words >= expected is solved, 0 and fewer is incomplete, timed_out wins over returncode, non-zero is error); fake_game via subprocess with FAKE_LLM_CALLS=2 prints 2 LLM lines, 2 tool lines and a parseable RESULT line, and FAKE_ALARM=429 puts `429` in its output; `cd public/b/mh_harness && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is green and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | grep -c ' ... ok'` is at least 8
After running the tests, `git status --short` shows no `__pycache__` entry (the .gitignore from B1-01 holds)
The suite is green: `.harness/check.sh` prints `check: lint ok · jest ok · build ok`

features.description: run_one.py starts one run through adapter.py, streams its output to a log, enforces timeout_s by killing the whole process tree, and appends one results.jsonl row; adapter.py's defaults run fake_game.py.
steps: `public/b/mh_harness/adapter.py` has exactly two functions each under a comment starting `# ADAPT:` that says what to fill in: `build_command(config, workdir)` returns `([sys.executable, <abs path of fake_game.py>], workdir)` by default, and `parse_result(log_text)` returns `{"words_found": n, "score": s}` from the last `RESULT {…}` line (words_found 0 and score None when there is none); `grep -c '# ADAPT:' public/b/mh_harness/adapter.py` prints 2 and the file has no other game-specific code

`python3 public/b/mh_harness/run_one.py CONFIG.json [--index K] [--round NAME]` (CONFIG.json holds one config object) creates `public/b/mh_harness/work/<name>-<K>/` (paths are relative to run_one.py's own directory, not the cwd, D46), starts the adapter's command with env = os.environ + config env + `HARNESS_WORKDIR` (absolute) + `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, with stdout and stderr redirected to `public/b/mh_harness/logs/<name>-<K>.log`, detached (POSIX `start_new_session=True`; Windows `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`), waits up to `timeout_s` (float allowed), on expiry calls `kill_tree` (POSIX os.killpg SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 2 s; Windows `taskkill /T /F /PID`), then appends one JSON line to `public/b/mh_harness/results.jsonl` with exactly the 16 fields name, index, round, config, words_found, score, wall_s, llm_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, llm_ms_median, tool_calls, repeated_tool_calls, exit_reason, error_tail, started_at (ISO 8601 UTC); `error_tail` is the last 20 log lines for `error`, else null; exit code 0 for solved/incomplete, 1 for timeout/error
SIGTERM or SIGINT to run_one kills the game tree and exits 130 without appending a row; `kill_tree`, `start_detached` and the main entry are the functions the plan names, so sweep.py can import them

`public/b/mh_harness/tests/test_run_one.py` cases (each in a tempdir via a `HARNESS_HOME` env override or a patched base dir, so the real results.jsonl is untouched): a run with FAKE_SLEEP_S=0.2 and FAKE_WORDS=2, expected_words 2 ends `solved` with wall_s > 0, llm_calls 3, tool_calls 3, and the log file contains the RESULT line; FAKE_WORDS=1 ends `incomplete`; FAKE_EXIT=2 ends `error` with error_tail a list of at most 20 strings whose last element is the RESULT line; FAKE_SLEEP_S=30 with timeout_s 1 ends `timeout` within 5 s and the child's pid is gone (`os.kill(pid, 0)` raises or, on POSIX, the process is a zombie reaped by wait); config env `FAKE_WORDS` reaches the child; the row has exactly the 16 field names; `cd public/b/mh_harness && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is green
The suite is green: `.harness/check.sh` prints `check: lint ok · jest ok · build ok`

features.description: sweep.py refuses unfilled placeholders, runs every config K times N at a time as run_one.py subprocesses, prints status lines with alarms, honours --dry-run and Ctrl-C, and prints the round's report table at the end.
steps: `python3 public/b/mh_harness/sweep.py public/b/mh_harness/configs/round1.json` exits 2 before starting any run with a message that names the config and the field, e.g. `refusing to start: config "base" field mcps[0] still has a placeholder: "<current set>"`; `ls public/b/mh_harness/logs public/b/mh_harness/work 2>/dev/null | grep -c base` prints 0 and results.jsonl is unchanged

`python3 public/b/mh_harness/sweep.py public/b/mh_harness/configs/fake-round.json --dry-run` prints one line per run with the argv and cwd (`cmd: … fake_game.py  cwd: …/work/base-0`) and runs nothing (no logs/ entries, no results.jsonl line)

`sweep.py CONFIGS.json [--parallel N] [--repeat K] [--interval S] [--alarm-after S] [--dry-run]` (defaults 4, 1, 15, 60): for each config and repeat index it writes the single config to `work/<name>-<K>/config.json` and starts `run_one.py` on it with `--index K --round <configs file stem>` via `start_detached` from run_one.py; at most N run at once; every `--interval` seconds it prints one line per live run `[<name>-<K>] <elapsed>s llm=<n> tools=<n>` by reading the run's log, appending ` ALARM: <reason>` when the log contains `429`, `rate limit`, `connection refused`, `address already in use` (case-insensitive) or `Traceback`, or `ALARM: no tool call after <alarm-after> s`; on KeyboardInterrupt it `kill_tree`s every live run_one and exits 130; when every run has ended it prints `report.py`'s table for this round (via `import report`; until B1-05 lands, a one-line `report: <n> runs ended` placeholder is acceptable and B1-05 replaces it)

`public/b/mh_harness/tests/test_sweep.py` cases: four configs with FAKE_SLEEP_S=2 and `--parallel 4` finish in under 5 s wall and leave 4 rows in the tempdir's results.jsonl; the placeholder refusal exits 2 with the config name and field in stderr and creates no work/ or logs/ entry; `--dry-run` prints 4 `cmd:` lines and writes nothing; FAKE_ALARM=429 with `--interval 0.5` makes the status output contain `ALARM: 429`; FAKE_SLEEP_S=3, FAKE_LLM_CALLS=1 with `--alarm-after 0.5 --interval 0.5` prints `ALARM: no tool call`; `--repeat 2` on one config leaves rows with index 0 and 1; `cd public/b/mh_harness && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is green
The suite is green: `.harness/check.sh` prints `check: lint ok · jest ok · build ok`

features.description: report.py summarises results.jsonl per config (medians across repeats), sorted by words found then wall time, with the noise, prod projection and pick sections in aligned text or markdown; sweep.py prints it after a round.
steps: `public/b/mh_harness/report.py` exports `load_rows(path, round_name=None)` (default round = the `round` of the last line), `summarise(rows, prod_cities=21) -> dict` (per name: words_found, wall_s, llm_calls, output_tokens, input_tokens, tool_calls, repeated_tool_calls as medians, exit reasons as `solved:2` style counts, plus noise, projection and pick) and `render(summary, md=False) -> str`; the CLI is `report.py [--round NAME] [--prod-cities 21] [--md]`; with no results.jsonl it prints `no results yet` and exits 0

Rows sort by words found desc then median wall s asc; under the table a `noise` section prints, per `control_of` pair, `base vs base_ctl: <gap> %` with ` NOISY` appended above 20 %; a `prod projection` section prints per config `<name>: ~<llm_calls / cities × prod_cities> LLM calls at <llm_ms_median> ms median`; a `pick` line names the top row whose every repeat is `solved`, or `pick: none solved every repeat`

`public/b/mh_harness/tests/test_report.py` builds rows in memory (no files) and checks: medians across three repeats (wall 10, 20, 90 gives 20); a config with 2 words beats one with 1 regardless of wall s and ties break by wall s; control gap 10 % is not NOISY and 25 % is; the projection for llm_calls 12, cities 6, prod_cities 21 is 42; the pick skips a config with one `incomplete` repeat; `--md` output starts with a `|` header row; `load_rows` picks the latest round by default; `cd public/b/mh_harness && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is green

`python3 public/b/mh_harness/sweep.py public/b/mh_harness/configs/fake-round.json --parallel 4 --interval 1` ends by printing the report table with four rows and `pick: base` (or whichever solved row has the lowest wall s), and `python3 public/b/mh_harness/report.py --md` prints the same round as a markdown table
The suite is green: `.harness/check.sh` prints `check: lint ok · jest ok · build ok`
